verdict.rationale: Terraform's docs say providers let it work with virtually any platform or service that has an accessible API, and that resources can span multiple cloud providers. The public Registry lets anyone publish and consume providers, which Terraform downloads automatically. Community users corroborate multi-service and cross-account management (Kubernetes, DNS, MySQL, cross-account AWS), though some report provider-dependency friction such as static providers and multi-step Kubernetes applies. Missing for 10: an explicit enumeration or count of covered major clouds and SaaS providers, and independent evidence of SaaS-provider breadth beyond cloud infrastructure.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage resources across all major clouds and SaaS providers through a broad provider ecosystem

citations.quote: Providers enable Terraform to work with virtually any platform or service with an accessible API.
You define resources, which may be across multiple cloud providers and services.
Anyone can publish and consume providers, modules, and policies on the public Terraform Registry.
Terraform can automatically download providers that are published on the Terraform Registry.
